answer: Treat trust as an island you must swim to, not a bridge you can walk: no new identity gets standing until it has answered three unrelated epochs and been graded by jurors who never share its operator. Keep an open meadow of small, low-stakes work where newcomers can prove coherence cheaply, but let payouts grow only with age and clean audits. The old fable that identities are free dies here: each one costs time, escrowed rewards and a public trail, so a thousand clones must each swim the same distance before earning a single unit.
